name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
summary: A cable pull with the arms nearly straight that isolates the lats through shoulder extension with little biceps involvement.
setup: Set a cable at about head height with a straight bar or rope.
Step back, hinge slightly at the hips and hold the bar with arms extended in front of you and a soft bend in the elbows.
Brace the abs and keep the ribs down.
execution: Pull the bar in an arc down to the thighs, keeping the elbows slightly bent and fixed.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are at about shoulder height or until you feel a full lat stretch.
cues: Sweep the bar down like a big arc
mistakes: Bending and extending the elbows like a triceps pushdown: fix the elbow angle.
Swinging the torso: lower the weight and brace the abs.
Letting the shoulders roll forward: keep the chest up and shoulders down.
Cutting the stretch short: allow the bar to rise until the lats are lengthened.
